recentItems.description:
The festive spirit of Christmas and New Year celebrations has begun in Visakhapatnam with an enthusiastic cake mixing ceremony at Dolphin Hotel. Hotel staff members joined guests in mixing a variety of dry fruits as part of the traditional cake preparation process. The event brought together guests and hospitality staff to celebrate the upcoming festive season.

Dolphin Hotel Associate Vice President Ramakrishna said the hotel has been organising the cake mixing ceremony every year as part of its festive tradition. The Executive Chef explained that the cake would be prepared using quality ingredients to ensure great taste and flavour. The event marked the beginning of the Christmas and New Year celebrations at the hotel, adding a festive touch to the atmosphere in Vizag.

recentItems.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India's economy remains strong despite the ongoing crisis in West Asia. Addressing the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, he highlighted the importance of renewable energy in strengthening India's energy security. Modi stated that India's energy situation would have been more challenging if the country had not expanded its renewable energy capacity over the past decade.

The Prime Minister said India's non-fossil fuel energy capacity has crossed 300 gigawatts and expressed confidence that the country will achieve its target of 500 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2030. He also highlighted India's position among the world's top three countries in the renewable energy sector. Emphasising stable policies for clean energy, Modi said investment opportunities worth more than ₹20 lakh crore are expected in the sector by the end of this decade. He underlined that clean energy will play a crucial role in ensuring India's energy security in the years ahead.

recentItems.description:
A mother from JNRM Colony in Gajuwaka, Visakhapatnam district, has appealed to the government to bring her son, Jetti Vamsi, back to India safely. According to his mother, Vamsi travelled to Russia in search of employment. After reportedly failing to find work there, he was allegedly deceived by a Nepali individual who promised him a better opportunity in Ukraine. The family claims that Vamsi was instead made to join the Russian Army. His mother has expressed deep concern for his safety and is urging the authorities to intervene and ensure his safe return to India. The family is seeking urgent assistance from the government to bring their son home.

recentItems.description:
Wars and conflicts across the world are increasingly affecting everyday life, even in countries far away from the battlefields. From rising petrol prices and LPG costs to grocery bills and economic uncertainty, the impact of international conflicts is reaching ordinary households.

Nearly eight decades after the establishment of the United Nations following World War II, the world continues to witness devastating conflicts. The Russia-Ukraine war, the destruction in Gaza, tensions involving Iran, Israel and the United States, Houthi attacks and growing instability across West Asia and Europe have raised serious concerns about global peace and security.

Although these wars involve specific countries and regions, their consequences are felt worldwide through fluctuations in crude oil prices, food security challenges, disruptions to international trade and rising living costs.

What is the United Nations doing to prevent these conflicts? Why are diplomatic efforts struggling to establish lasting peace? Who has the power to stop these wars, and is there a possible solution?

Watch today's special edition of Pratidhwani for an in-depth analysis of global conflicts, their economic consequences and the challenges facing the international community.

recentItems.title: ఎన్నికల కౌంటింగ్ ఏజెంట్లకు పోలీసుల కీలక సూచనలు | DSP Hanumantha Rao Reviews Counting Centre Security
recentItems.description:
Elaborate arrangements have been made for the Chilakaluripet Municipal Election counting scheduled for Tuesday in Palnadu district. Narasaraopet DSP Hanumantha Rao inspected the counting arrangements at AMG College and confirmed that tight security measures are in place. Five counting halls have been arranged in a single building, with dedicated strong rooms and security personnel. A total of 200 police officers and staff will be deployed to ensure peaceful counting. The counting for the chairperson post and 48 wards is planned to be completed in three rounds.
